title: Texas AG sues OpenAI and Altman over ChatGPT harm to minors
subtitle: The 67-page petition invokes Texas's Deceptive Trade Practices Act and SCOPE Act, cites two teenage deaths tied to ChatGPT use, and asks the court to bar new model releases in Texas without approval from a court-appointed evaluator.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton filed a 67-page petition in Collin County on October 23 against six OpenAI entities and CEO Sam Altman, alleging deceptive marketing of ChatGPT's safety and inadequate protections for minors. The suit invokes the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act and the state's SCOPE Act, which requires platforms accessible to Texas minors to implement age verification and parental controls. Civil penalties under the DTPA run $10,000 per violation; the petition requests more than $1 million plus a permanent injunction.

The requested relief is unusually aggressive. Beyond money, Paxton asks the court to block minors' access to ChatGPT in Texas and to prohibit OpenAI from releasing new ChatGPT models in Texas without first obtaining approval from a court-appointed independent evaluator. If granted, that order would make Texas the first US jurisdiction with pre-release judicial review of frontier-model deployments. The petition cites the suicide of 16-year-old Adam Raine, whose family alleges ChatGPT provided active assistance in planning, and the overdose death of 19-year-old Sam Nelson. These are allegations and will be contested; OpenAI has not yet filed a response.

This is the second state-level offensive in two weeks. Eight state attorneys general filed a coordinated action on October 14, and Florida has a separate suit already pending. What is new in the Texas filing is the SCOPE Act hook: product-liability and consumer-protection theories against general-purpose chatbots have been attempted before, but SCOPE grounds the case in a specific statutory duty around minors that chatbot vendors have mostly treated as applying only to social platforms. If a Texas court agrees SCOPE applies to ChatGPT, every general-purpose assistant becomes a SCOPE-regulated service in Texas overnight, which would reshape age-verification engineering across the industry.

A note for learners: regulation of frontier AI in the US is not arriving through Congress; it is arriving through state attorneys general and consumer-protection statutes written for other things. If you work on product, trust and safety, or policy, read the SCOPE Act and the DTPA directly — not the news summaries. The specific definitions of 'covered platform' and the state's standard for 'deceptive' are what will actually determine which products are reshaped by rulings like this one.
